content_preview.title: Trump Names Jay Clayton to Lead Super Intelligence Force as Executive Order Replaces 'AI' in Federal Documents
content_preview.summary: Trump formed a Super Intelligence Force chaired by DNI Jay Clayton with a 120-day reporting window, days after an order renaming AI in executive-branch documents.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

President Donald Trump has formed a "Super Intelligence Force" led by National Intelligence Director Jay Clayton, according to [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/04/trump-unveils-his-new-super-intelligence-force/), with a charter that includes a 120-day reporting window. The announcement follows a [September 29 executive order](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/09/inaugurating-the-era-of-super-intelligence/) that directs federal agencies to say "Super Int...

editor_notes.content_quality: 693-word News article (range 400-1200) with clear separation between what the executive order directs (its own section, quoting the order text), what Trump said (quoted from TechCrunch and NBC News), and what is only reported (WSJ-sourced vice chairs and the 120-day window, relayed by TechCrunch and flagged as 'reportedly'). A 'What We Don't Know' section covers the title discrepancy, the unpublished charter, and the future statutory definition. Neutral tone, no characterization of the policy's merits beyond sourced quotes.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three snapshots from disk (gunzip, text-extracted); all status 200, no archive fallback, suspicious_patterns null for all three. source-0 (TechCrunch, Anthony Ha, Oct 4): confirms Trump's Truth Social quote verbatim ('is tasked with coordinating the effort of the Federal Government to ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence'), Clayton to lead, 'The Wall Street Journal reports that Clayton will chair... with Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson, Undersecretary of War for Research and Engineering Emil Michael, and Office of Personnel Management Director Scott Kupor serving as vice chairs' (three vice chairs), 'The task force will reportedly have 120 days to create a report on the risks and opportunities presented by AI', and the charter quote 'develop plans for responding to SI-enabled threats to our society, while preventing overregulation and regulatory capture that would stifle innovation and competition' ('reportedly'). source-1 (NBC News, Raquel Coronell Uribe, Oct 4): confirms 'Undersecretary of Defense for Research and Engineering Emil Michael', reporting line to Trump and Susie Wiles, both Truth Social quotes verbatim ('Following the Historic White House Accord on Super Intelligence...' and 'will coordinate the Federal Government's engagement with Consumers, Public Interest Groups, Religious Organizations, Critical Infrastructure Providers, and Super Intelligence Companies'), and the Sacks statement. source-2 (whitehouse.gov, Executive Order, September 29, 2026): Sec. 1 policy that the executive branch 'shall use the terms Super Intelligence and SI in place of Artificial Intelligence and AI' 'to the maximum extent permitted by law'; Sec. 2(a) quoted list 'official correspondence, public communications, websites, reports, policy documents, and other non-statutory documents within the executive branch' verbatim; Sec. 2(b) 'Nothing in this section requires the alteration of previously issued regulations, Presidential actions, contracts, grants, or other historical documents' verbatim; Sec. 3(a) definition by reference to 15 U.S.C. 9401(3); Sec. 3(b) 60 days for APST to submit proposed legislative language; Sec. 4(c) 'enforceable at law or in equity' verbatim. The executive order text does NOT create a task force, name Clayton or any vice chair, or contain a 120-day deadline; the article correctly attributes those only to TechCrunch/NBC and does not attribute them to the order. The order text carries an order number (14434) that the article does not state; no unverified order number appears in the article. The order text names no one other than the APST title and does not mention Emil Michael, so the title discrepancy is correctly presented as a TechCrunch vs NBC difference without choosing one. whitehouse.gov, techcrunch.com and nbcnews.com are all already in config/source_allowlist.txt; no allowlist change needed.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All names, titles, dates and quotes verified verbatim against the snapshots. Each of the three statements about the order is confirmed exactly: it mandates 'Super Intelligence'/'SI' terminology in non-statutory executive-branch documents 'to the maximum extent permitted by law'; it keeps the statutory definition of artificial intelligence (15 U.S.C. 9401(3)) as the governing definition; and it exempts previously issued regulations, Presidential actions, contracts, grants and other historical documents. Cross-references verified: /article/2026-09/22-trump-announces-ai-force-and-plans-to-name-an-ai-czar-offering-no-details-on-its-authority and /article/2026-09/30-trump-and-six-ai-company-chiefs-sign-voluntary-frontier-accord-... both exist on disk and are accurately characterized (the Sept 22 'AI Force' announcement; the Sept 30 voluntary accord).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Distinguishes directed actions from official statements. Short Analysis section stays close to the order text.
editor_notes.originality: The Sept 22 article covered Trump's AI Force proposal with no structure or authority; the Sept 30 accord article covered the voluntary frontier accord and mentioned the executive order only in one sentence via Cointelegraph. Neither names Clayton or the vice chairs, reports the task force announcement, or analyzes the order text (terminology scope, statutory definition, exemptions, 60-day legislative deadline). The follow-up override is justified: this is genuinely new substance, not a rehash.
concerns: The title says the order 'Replaces' AI in 'Federal Documents'; the order directs use of the new terms in non-statutory executive-branch documents to the maximum extent permitted by law and exempts historical documents. The body states these limits precisely, so the headline is shorthand rather than a misstatement.

The vice-chair list is attributed to 'TechCrunch ... the same report' while TechCrunch itself attributes it to the Wall Street Journal; the article does not name the WSJ. Attribution to TechCrunch is accurate but second-hand, and Kupor appears in only one source.
The Analysis paragraph (practical effect limited to vocabulary) is an interpretation, though grounded in the order's own text; it is hedged and appropriate.
recommendations: Where a source relays another outlet's reporting, name the original outlet (here the Wall Street Journal) in the attribution.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully sourced, and the primary-source order text is quoted correctly and its limits conveyed. APPROVE.
